Discovered during LP-0MSND8QJ6006RYGR (llm project: Verify caching active and audit skill routing) — parent LP-0MSLQCGH0001US3G (Ensure test results are cached), discovered-from:LP-0MSND8QJ6006RYGR.

## Summary
run_tests.py (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py) resolves its target repo from its OWN install location (REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] = the SorraAgents framework repo), not from the invoking project. The CLI (main -> run_all without cwd -> cwd = cwd or REPO_ROOT) therefore runs/caches the FRAMEWORK repo's suite when invoked from any other project.

## Evidence (from llm repo, cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/llm)
- 'python3 /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --summary --suite pytest' printed '8 failed, 1814 passed' — that is the SORRAAGENTS suite (llm's suite is 2130 passed, exit 0).
- '--json --suite pytest' returned cached=True returncode=1 — reading the SorraAgents cache, not the llm cache.
- The audit skill compensates correctly: TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel at import; passes cwd=str(project_root) to query_cached/run_cached, so the llm cache entries are written/read via the audit path only.

## Impact
An agent or operator following the test skill's documented invocation (python3 ./scripts/run_tests.py --json) from a non-framework project tests and caches the WRONG repo's suite. Cross-project consumers must remember to pass cwd explicitly (audit does; ship/implement pass cwd where relevant).

## Proposed fix (minimal)
Detect the invoking project root from cwd at CLI time — e.g. 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' from os.getcwd() when --cwd is not passed (mirroring audit_runner.TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT), falling back to REPO_ROOT. Preserve existing behavior when invoked from the framework repo itself. Alternatively add a --project-root flag and document it in the test skill SKILL.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] run_tests.py CLI run from a non-framework project (e.g. llm) targets that project's repo + cache (git-state fingerprint at that project's HEAD), not SorraAgents.
- [ ] Invoked from the framework repo itself, behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Audit skill read-only auto-verification (query_cached at TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT) still hits the same cache entries.
- [ ] Test skill SKILL.md documents the project-root resolution (and any --project-root flag).

## Plan: changelog
- 2026-09-27: `/skill:plan` auto-complete path (effort Extra Small / risk Low). Six review stages run against existing content; added `**Key Files:**` section (completeness). Plan marked `plan_complete`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — project-root detection, `--project-root` flag, cwd threading
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — documents project-root resolution
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — resolution semantics and cache location
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` — detection/override tests

# [IMPL] Harden proxy-compaction-bridge against stale ctx

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-compaction-bridge` to no-op when
the captured `ctx` has been invalidated by a session replacement, so its
handlers never throw `This extension ctx is stale ...` and never crash or
degrade an unrelated run.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 and part of AC5.

## Scope

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`: both the
  `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers call
  `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` — a stale ctx throws.
- Move the session-id resolution into a stale-safe helper in the dependency-free
  core `compaction-bridge.js` (e.g. `safeSessionId(ctx)` returning `null` when
  access throws). The adapter must:
  - `after_provider_response`: no-op when the session id cannot be resolved.
  - `context`: return `undefined` (pass through messages unchanged) when the
    session id cannot be resolved.
- Never let a stale-ctx throw escape a handler; never mutate dispatch on an
  unknown session.
- Update `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` to document the stale-ctx
  fail-safe behaviour.
- Preserve the compaction-bridge wire contract (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) and the
  existing dispatch reshape semantics exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stale-ctx stub, both handlers do not throw; `context` returns
   `undefined` (passthrough) and `after_provider_response` performs no state
   update.
- With a live ctx, behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing
   compaction/reshape tests continue to pass, wire contract intact).
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` documents the stale-ctx fail-safe
   path and this work item.
- The stale-ctx regression tests added by the test item pass (green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `safeSessionId(ctx)` (try/catch around `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()`)
  to `compaction-bridge.js` and export it.
- Use it in the two `index.ts` handlers with early return.
- Add the docs paragraph.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **[TEST] Stale-ctx regression tests for pi-client extensions**.

## Deliverables

- Stale-safe `proxy-compaction-bridge` handlers.
- Documented fail-safe behaviour.
- Green stale-ctx regression tests.

**Key Files:**
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`

# [IMPL] Harden proxy-sse-signals against stale ctx

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-sse-signals` to no-op when its
captured UI handle (`statusUi`) belongs to an invalidated ctx, so a
session-replacement cannot make its async capturing-fetch callback throw and
crash or degrade an unrelated run.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 and part of AC5.

## Scope

- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts`: `turn_start` captures
  `ctx.hasUI ? ctx.ui : null`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls
  `statusUi.setStatus(...)` and `turn_end` calls `ctx.ui.setStatus(...)` — both
  can hit a stale ctx/UI handle.
- Add a stale-safe status helper in the dependency-free core `sse-signals.js`
  (e.g. `safeSetStatus(ui, key, text)` that swallows/guards stale-ctx throws
  and reports whether the write happened) and use it from the adapter so a
  stale handle is a silent no-op.
- `turn_end` must not throw when the ctx/UI is stale; clearing the local handle
  must still occur.
- Preserve SSE signal parsing/formatting behaviour and the passthrough of bytes
  through the capturing fetch unchanged.
- Update `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/README.md` (or code comments) to document
  the stale-ctx fail-safe behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stale-ctx stub, the captured-status path and `turn_end` do not throw;
   the status write is skipped and the local handle is cleared.
- With a live ctx, signal rendering behaviour is unchanged (existing
   `sse-signals` tests pass; bytes still pass through unwrapped).
- Stale-ctx fail-safe behaviour is documented in the extension README/comments
   with a reference to this work item.
- The stale-ctx regression tests added by the test item pass (green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `safeSetStatus(ui, key, text)` to `sse-signals.js` and export it.
- Use it in `index.ts` for both the callback and `turn_end`; always clear the
  captured handle in `turn_end`.
- Add the docs note.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **[TEST] Stale-ctx regression tests for pi-client extensions**.

## Deliverables

- Stale-safe `proxy-sse-signals` status handling.
- Documented fail-safe behaviour.
- Green stale-ctx regression tests.

**Key Files:**
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/sse-signals.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/README.md`
- `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`

## Summary

The audit runner's Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest omits the audited item's **committed** touched files whenever the working tree is clean, causing false "outside the manifest" / `unmet` verdicts for criteria whose implementation and tests live in those committed files.

Discovered during the audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (log: `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX_20260927T095408.log`).

## Evidence

- The audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX returned `Ready to close: No` with parent AC1 `partial`, AC2 `unmet`, AC3 `unmet` — each justified by wording such as "`test_cache._default_runner`/`run_tests.py` are outside the provided manifest" and "test_cache is outside the manifest so its runner cannot be verified".
- The item's implementation commit `a83ada6a` changed 14 files (`git show --stat a83ada6a`): `.githooks/pre-push`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py`, `skill/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_implement_sys_path_resolution.py`, `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`.
- `git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --name-only` returns all of those files, so the data is available — the manifest simply did not use it.
- The manifest actually used contained only `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`; the latter is **not** in `a83ada6a`.
- The working tree was clean at audit time (`git status --porcelain` showed only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

## Root cause

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:4351`) builds the manifest's file list from:

1. the description's Key Files (`_extract_key_files`);
2. `_git_changed_files()` (`audit_runner.py:4210`) — `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain=v1`, i.e. **working-tree / untracked changes only**;
3. Phase 1 evidence `file:line` refs;
4. a lightweight repo index.

It does **not** use `_resolve_touched_files()` (`audit_runner.py:1476`), which already resolves the union of (a) files in commits referencing the item id (`git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=<id> --name-only`), (b) comment-recorded commit hashes, and (c) Key Files — the correct source for a fully-committed item on a clean checkout.

Consequently, when an item's work is committed and the tree is clean (the normal post-implementation state), `_git_changed_files()` contributes nothing and the manifest collapses to the Phase 1 evidence refs + repo index. The `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` fail-fast guard (`audit_runner.py:1231`) does not abort because the manifest does reference *some* item-repo file, even though it omits the item's actual touched files.

## Desired behaviour

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` must include the audited item's committed touched files (via `_resolve_touched_files()`), so a clean checkout still yields a manifest covering the item's real changes. The fail-fast scope validation must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_build_file_scope_manifest()` includes the audited item's committed touched files (reuse `_resolve_touched_files()`), in addition to the working-tree diff, Key Files, Phase 1 refs, and repo index.
- [ ] Regression test: with a clean working tree and a committed commit whose message references the item id, the built manifest contains that commit's changed files.
- [ ] A scope-validation regression test asserts that a manifest which references the item repo but omits the item's touched files is rejected (or is impossible to build).
- [ ] Re-auditing SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX after this fix no longer reports its ACs as "outside the manifest" solely because the item's files are committed rather than uncommitted.
- [ ] Full suite green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py — `_build_file_scope_manifest`, `_git_changed_files`, `_resolve_touched_files`, `_validate_file_scope_manifest`
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — the audit whose false-negative verdicts surfaced this defect.
- Blocks the accurate re-audit/closure of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (dependency edge recorded).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (RESOLVED) — Does AC3 require hardening `_validate_file_scope_manifest()`, or is the "impossible to build" regression test sufficient? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** AC3 says a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files must be "rejected (or is impossible to build)". The Desired-behaviour section separately states the fail-fast scope validation "must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files", which reads as a validator-hardening requirement.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** harden `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` with an optional `touched_files` argument: when a non-empty touched set is resolvable and none of its paths appear in the manifest, return a scope error; when the set is `None`/empty, fail open (preserves current behaviour for mono-repo/unknown cases). Plan child SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O covers this; the regression test is delivered either way.
- **Alternative A:** satisfy AC3 solely with the "impossible to build" regression test (no validator change).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **harden**. `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` gains an optional `touched_files` argument that returns a scope error when a non-empty resolved touched set has no path in the manifest, and fails open when the set is `None`/empty. Delivered by SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O; the regression test is still required.

### Q2 (RESOLVED) — The item's `effort`/`risk` fields are lowercase ("medium"/"medium"), so the plan-approval gate's documented Medium-effort trigger did not fire. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `should_request_plan_approval()` compares `effort` case-sensitively against `{"Medium", "Large", "Extra Large"}`. `wl show` reports this item's values as `"medium"`/`"medium"` (other items, e.g. SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX, use `"Medium"`/`"Severe"`). `plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` therefore returned `request_approval: false`, skipping the human checkpoint the skill documents for Medium effort.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** correct the item's `effort`/`risk` to canonical capitalised values and, if plan sign-off is wanted, review the child breakdown before implementation. (Making the gate case-insensitive is a separate change, out of scope here.)
- **Alternative A:** accept the gate result as-is and proceed without a producer approval pause (what this run did).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **correct**. The item's `effort`/`risk` were set to the canonical capitalised values (`Medium`/`Medium`) via `wl update`. With the corrected data, `plan-approval-gate` returns `request_approval: true` ("its effort is Medium scale"), so the plan is surfaced to the producer for sign-off before implementation.

### Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — `extract_acceptance_criteria()` only exits the AC section on an `##` heading, so an H1-headed description makes the AC-coverage review treat Key Files / Related-work bullets as ACs and recommend `stop`. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` detects the AC header with `^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria` but breaks only on `^##\s+`. This plan normalised this item's and its children's headings to `##` (conformant with the AGENTS.md `## Acceptance Criteria` convention) so coverage parses correctly. Tracked as discovered-from work item SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** reaffirm the H2 convention for descriptions and make the extractor break on any heading level 1–6 for robustness.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — informational; no plan decision depends on it._

### Plan approval (2026-09-27)

- **Decision:** APPROVED — producer replied "LGTM" to the four-child, test-first plan (SA-0MUKCOQI10095463 → SA-0MUKCOUXN001VH47 → SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O → SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6). The plan-approval gate (Medium effort) is satisfied; `needsProducerReview` is cleared and the plan is ready for implementation.
data.title: Audit FILE SCOPE manifest omits a clean tree's committed touched files, causing false out-of-scope verdicts

## Summary

Add failing (red) regression tests that pin the FILE SCOPE manifest's inclusion of the audited item's **committed** touched files for a clean working tree. This is the test-first half of parent bug SA-0MUJNZ5RN0078B5M: without the fix, `_build_file_scope_manifest()` contributes nothing from git when the tree is clean, so the manifest omits the item's real changes.

## Target outcome

A deterministic, hermetic test that fails on the current `_build_file_scope_manifest()` and passes once committed touched files are included.

## Definition of done (pass/fail + automated tests)

- New tests in `skill/audit/tests/` (extend `test_audit_runner_phase2.py` or add `test_audit_runner_file_scope.py`) using the existing mocked-runner convention (no live git).
- A test where the working tree is clean (`git diff --name-only HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` produce no entries) but `git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=<id> --name-only` returns the item's committed files; assert every returned file appears in the built manifest.
- A test asserting the manifest still includes Key Files, Phase 1 evidence refs, and the repository index sections (no regression of existing composition).
- A test asserting graceful degradation: when `_resolve_touched_files` yields `None` (git unavailable / nothing recorded), the manifest is still non-empty (Key Files/index) and does not raise.
- Run: `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2.py -q`. The new committed-files test MUST be observed red before C2 lands; capture the red output in a work-item comment.

## Constraints

- Hermetic: inject a fake runner; never shell out to real git or mutate the live worklog.
- Test-only deliverable: do not change production code in this item (the failing test is the point).

## Risky assumptions

- The manifest builder can be exercised directly with an injected runner (it already accepts `runner=`).
- The mocked-runner convention in `test_audit_runner_phase2.py` can express "clean tree + committed log output".

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_build_file_scope_manifest`, `_resolve_touched_files`, `_git_changed_files`)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test with a clean working tree and a committed `git log --grep` hit asserts the built manifest contains that commit's changed files.
- [ ] A test asserts the manifest still contains Key Files, Phase 1 refs, and repo index entries.
- [ ] A test asserts the manifest builds non-empty and raises nothing when touched-file resolution returns `None`.
- [ ] The new committed-files test is observed red against the unfixed `_build_file_scope_manifest()` and the red output is captured in a work-item comment.

## Dependencies

- None (first child; test-first).

# Intake Brief: Misleading completion message on LLM summaries

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report renderer (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) always concludes with "This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}." regardless of whether the skill actually completed successfully — the AC verdict column may show "unmet" but the conclusion line remains positive, creating a misleading impression.

## Users

- **AI agents** running skills — they rely on the report to know whether further action is needed.
- **Producers** reviewing work items — they need clear signals about whether the skill session succeeded or requires re-run.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The conclusion line in `render_report` reflects the actual outcome: use "completed" when all acceptance criteria are met, and "incomplete" (or similar) when any criterion is unmet or a failure occurred.
2. When the outcome is incomplete, the message includes a clear indication of required action (e.g., "requires attention" or "ready for re-run").
3. When the outcome is completed, the message retains the "Ready for {next_action}" phrasing (unchanged behaviour for successful runs).
4. All existing tests in `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` pass after the change.
5. The report header line (`# Completed {skill_name}`) is consistent with the actual outcome — if incomplete, the header should reflect that (e.g., `# Incomplete {skill_name}` or similar).

## Constraints

- Must remain backwards compatible with all callers (library usage and CLI mode).
- The `acceptance_criteria` parameter is already passed to `render_report`; the change must derive status from this without requiring new parameters.
- The change must not alter the structure of the metadata, producer actions, or notes sections.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` in `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` always outputs:
  - Header: `# Completed {skill_name}`
  - Conclusion: `This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}.`
- AC verdicts are passed as `(ac#, description, metric, verdict)` tuples where `verdict` is `"met"` or `"unmet"`.
- `derive_status()` in `shared/herdr_pane` already exists and can determine session status from ACs/producer actions/notes.

## Desired change

- Derive a session status (completed/incomplete) from the `acceptance_criteria` parameter.
- Condition the header and conclusion text on this status.
- For incomplete sessions: surface a clear "incomplete" status and indicate what action is needed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Core change: condition header and conclusion on AC verdicts.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Tests for the new conditional behaviour.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — May need to expose a function to derive completion status from ACs for reuse.

## Related work

- **SA-0MM1AWO6D1RVZF3I** — "Define abort behavior and messaging" (blocked) — related theme (abort messaging) but scoped to the cleanup skill specifically; this work addresses the general report renderer.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Backwards compatibility** — Callers relying on the current "Completed" header unchanged when ACs are all met.
- **Empty AC list** — When no ACs are supplied, the renderer currently shows a placeholder row. Assumption: empty AC list + no producer actions + no notes = "completed"; any producer actions or notes = "incomplete".
- **Scope** — Some skills may have inline completion messages outside `render_report`. Scope is limited to `render_report.py`; other files are noted as a potential follow-up.
- **Scope creep** — General messaging improvements across all skills are out of scope; this addresses only the report renderer.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the header (`# Completed {skill_name}`) also change when incomplete, or only the conclusion? — **Answer (agent analysis):** Both should change for consistency. The header should read `# Incomplete {skill_name}` (or similar) when any AC is unmet. Source: design analysis.
- Q: What constitutes "incomplete" — any single unmet AC, or a threshold (e.g., more than 50% unmet)? — **Answer (work item description):** Any unmet AC or failure should be treated as incomplete. The description states "meaning the skill needs to be run again or the producer has an action." Source: work-item description.
- Q: Should producer-actions or notes also influence the status (e.g., notes indicating a known blocker)? — **Answer (agent analysis):** Notes can indicate context but should not override AC verdicts. Producer actions needing attention is an additional signal but AC verdicts are the primary determinant. Source: design analysis.
data.title: Misleading completion message on LLM summaries
